title: Diagonal and graph evaluation of composed coefficient mates
statement:
Let $B$ be a scheme, let $u:V\to B$ and $w:W\to B$ be objects of the small pro-étale site with the universe convention of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $h:W\to V$ be a $B$-morphism with $w=u\circ h$. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], with coefficient rings $\Lambda_Z=p_Z^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the canonical coefficient maps $\alpha_f$ and their mates $\eta_f$ of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms, def-sfb-eta], with the composition comparisons fixed by [lem-sfb-eta-comp]. Put $P=V\times_BV$, regarded as an object over $V$ by its second projection, let $\delta:V\to P$ be the diagonal, and put $\gamma=(h,\mathrm{id}_W):W\to V\times_BW$. Identify $P\times_VW$ with $V\times_BW$ using the pushforward-composition isomorphism of [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp], whose scheme map sends $(v_1,v_2,z)$ to $(v_1,z)$ with $v_2=h(z)$.

For every $s\in\Lambda_B(V)$ the following identity of sections of $\Lambda_W$ at $W/W$ holds:
$$\Lambda_W(\gamma)\eta_{w,V}(s)=\eta_{h,V}\bigl(\Lambda_V(\delta)\eta_{u,V}(s)\bigr).$$
Here $\eta_{u,V}(s)\in\Lambda_V(P)$ and $\eta_{w,V}(s)\in\Lambda_W(V\times_BW)$; the target of $\eta_{h,V}$ is identified with $\Lambda_W(W)$ by $V\times_VW\cong W$. Under the same fibre-product comparison, the base change of $\delta$ along $h$ is precisely $\gamma$. This holds without any monomorphism or constant-section hypothesis.

proof.text: Write $Q=P\times_VW$ (using the second projection $P\to V$) and $R=V\times_BW$. The base-change description of pushforward [def-sfb-finite-lower-star] and its composition comparison [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp] use the isomorphism $e:Q\xrightarrow{\sim}R$ with formulas $e(v_1,v_2,z)=(v_1,z)$ and $e^{-1}(v,z)=(v,h(z),z)$. These formulas mean maps induced by the displayed projections, not merely maps of underlying point sets: their existence follows from $w=u\circ h$, and their composites have the identity projections, hence are identities by the fibre-product universal property. Let $D=V\times_VW$ and identify $D\cong W$ by the second projection, with inverse $(h,\mathrm{id}_W)$. Base-changing $\delta$ gives $\delta_W:D\to Q$; under this identification write $j:W\to Q$, so $j(z)=(h(z),h(z),z)$. The projections give $e\circ j=(h,\mathrm{id}_W)=\gamma$, equivalently $e^{-1}\circ\gamma=j$. This proves the geometric clause. All restrictions here are morphisms in the relevant small sites: base change is the functor in [def-sfb-finite-lower-star], and morphisms of the sites are the base-scheme morphisms [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

source.place: final paragraph: canonical iterated-fibre-product comparison, specialized to f=h, g=u; explicit base-changed diagonal

proof.text:
Put $a=\eta_{u,V}(s)\in\Lambda_V(P)$ and $t=\eta_{h,P}(a)\in\Lambda_W(Q)$. Apply [lem-sfb-eta-comp] with $f=h:W\to V$ and $g=u:V\to B$, so that $g\circ f=w$. Evaluate its equality at the site object $V\to B$ and then at $s$. By [def-sfb-finite-lower-star], the component of $u_*(\eta_h)$ at $V$ is the component $\eta_{h,P}$. By [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp], the remaining comparison sends sections on $Q$ to sections on $R$; since restriction is contravariant its component is $\Lambda_W(e^{-1})$. Consequently
$$\eta_{w,V}(s)=\Lambda_W(e^{-1})(t).$$
The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-eta-comp] are met: $h,u$ are scheme morphisms, $\Lambda$ is a commutative condensed ring, and the coefficient maps and composition comparisons use the normalization specified there.

source.place: paragraph 3: coefficient-mate composition, evaluated on V and s

proof.text:
By [def-sfb-eta], $\eta_h:\Lambda_V\to h_*\Lambda_W$ is a morphism of abelian sheaves, hence its underlying presheaf morphism commutes with restrictions. Apply its defining naturality square to the $V$-site morphism $\delta:V\to P$ and to $a\in\Lambda_V(P)$. Pushforward is restriction along base change [def-sfb-finite-lower-star], so the restriction of $h_*\Lambda_W$ along $\delta$ is $\Lambda_W(\delta_W)$, with target $\Lambda_W(D)$. Thus
$$\Lambda_W(\delta_W)(t)=\eta_{h,V}\bigl(\Lambda_V(\delta)(a)\bigr).$$
After the same identification $D\cong W$ as in step 1 this is
$$\Lambda_W(j)(t)=\eta_{h,V}\bigl(\Lambda_V(\delta)(a)\bigr).$$
This is just naturality of the sheaf morphism already specified by the cited definition; it uses no localization equivalence or theorem identifying inverse image with restriction.

source.place: paragraphs 1 and 3: eta is a sheaf morphism; its defining naturality square at the diagonal

proof.text:
Restrict the equality in step 2 along $\gamma$. Contravariant functoriality and $e^{-1}\circ\gamma=j$ from step 1 give
$$\Lambda_W(\gamma)\eta_{w,V}(s)
=\Lambda_W(\gamma)\Lambda_W(e^{-1})(t)
=\Lambda_W(e^{-1}\circ\gamma)(t)
=\Lambda_W(j)(t).$$
Insert step 3 and $a=\eta_{u,V}(s)$ to obtain precisely
$$\Lambda_W(\gamma)\eta_{w,V}(s)=\eta_{h,V}\bigl(\Lambda_V(\delta)\eta_{u,V}(s)\bigr).$$
Every equality is in $\Lambda_W(W)$ under the stated final-object identification. The argument never requires either site morphism to be a monomorphism and never restricts $s$ to constant sections.
